name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3419
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: Nut captures Long Island bird

indicators.note: something that captures holds another thing inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a pecan is a nut
LI is the standard abbreviation for Long Island, New York

explanation.surface: A squirrel or a crazy person on Long Island grabs a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' could be a madman in the surface, but here it is the edible kind; LI is a standard US abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a throat pouch for scooping fish.

clue.text: Dance and leap about conclusion of Seascape (America's classic play)

indicators.note: a conclusion is an end, so only the last letter of the word is kept
about means surrounding, so the first pieces wrap around the rest

blocks.note: a prom is a formal school dance
last letter of the word
America's read as 'the US'
to bound is to leap

explanation.surface: A dance-and-leap staging of Albee's play Seascape, an American classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America's classic play' reads as one phrase, but America's is wordplay and only 'classic play' is the definition; Seascape merely gives its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prometheus Bound is the ancient Greek tragedy, traditionally credited to Aeschylus, of the Titan chained to a rock.

clue.text: Woman in radical daily

indicators.note: a radical change is a thorough one, so these letters are completely reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman featured in a left-wing newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a female given name, so it can stand for any woman.

clue.text: Put tin on half-dead, tailless experimenter's rodent — that might shed some light on matters

definitions.text: that might shed some light on matters

indicators.note: half means only one of two equal parts survives, so the back half is dropped
without a tail, the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to can food is to seal it in a tin
taken as written
a lab rat is the rodent used in laboratory experiments

explanation.surface: A grisly lab scene, tinning a half-dead rat for an experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN, then DE from half of dead, then LAB RAT without its tail: CANDELABRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A candelabra is a branched holder for several candles, which literally sheds light.

clue.text: Southwesterner's backhanded exclamation upon noticing a vehicle

indicators.note: a backhanded remark goes the wrong way round, so the words are read in reverse

blocks.note: what you might cry on spotting a van: 'Oh, a van!'

explanation.surface: Someone from the Southwest makes a snide remark on spotting a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken cry 'Oh, a van!' is reversed whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navaho, or Navajo, are a Native American people of Arizona, New Mexico and Utah.

clue.text: Like some architecture degrees involving a certain rental, mostly

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it, so one piece sits inside the other
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: BAs, Bachelor of Arts degrees
U-Haul is an American truck and trailer rental company

explanation.surface: Architecture qualifications that somehow include renting something.
explanation.walkthrough: U-Haul loses its last letter and sits inside BAS, giving BAUHAUS. 'A certain rental' points to a brand name, not a generic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bauhaus was the German design school whose name labels a stark modernist style of building.

clue.text: Salami, processed in ancient times like some vinegar

indicators.note: processed food has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged
in tells us the rearranged letters go inside another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
BC, before Christ, marks dates in ancient times

explanation.surface: Cured sausage made the old-fashioned way, pickled in vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsamic vinegar is the dark, sweet Italian kind aged from grape must.

clue.text: Powerful narcotic envelops bone

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap around, so the answer is wrapped inside the words before it

blocks.note: the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A strong drug wrapped around a bone, like a hidden stash.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the human forearm.

clue.text: The things that make life comfortable absolutely include, in the first place, shoelaces

definitions.text: The things that make life comfortable

indicators.note: in the first place points to the opening position, so only the initial letter is kept

blocks.note: amen as an exclamation of agreement: absolutely, so be it
first letter of the word
ties are things that fasten, like shoelaces

explanation.surface: A claim that comfort starts, above all, with good shoelaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' looks like a link joining two ideas, but it only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are the conveniences and facilities that add ease and pleasure to living.

clue.text: Dog relapsing after repeated exposure to its parts

indicators.text: after repeated exposure to its parts
indicators.note: the word's parts are put on show again and again, so its letters are reused and reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written: nine letters, each used at least once
six of the nine letters of relapsing are each brought out a second time

explanation.surface: A dog keeps falling back into bad habits after being exposed to something.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a letter bank: the answer uses only the nine letters of relapsing, every one of them, with S, P, R, I, N and E each appearing twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer spaniel is a gundog breed, bred to flush or spring game birds.

clue.text: Prosperous, after losing $1,000 from the distant past

indicators.note: after losing tells us a word has had something taken away from it

blocks.note: a golden age or golden opportunity is a prosperous one
G, short for grand, is slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: Someone who was wealthy until they lost a thousand dollars, long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Take G away from GOLDEN and OLDEN remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned adjective for bygone times, as in 'olden days'.

clue.text: True love doesn't run smooth, taking in neutral person who's willing

indicators.note: a course that doesn't run smooth is disordered, so these letters get rearranged
taking in means admitting something inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: taken as written
N stands for neutral, as on a gear stick or an electric plug

explanation.surface: A twist on Shakespeare's line that the course of true love never did run smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows from A Midsummer Night's Dream; 'doesn't run smooth' scrambles TRUE LOVE, and N slips in to make VOLUNTEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A volunteer offers to do something freely, the very picture of willingness.

clue.text: Times here adapted ad for classic cult film

indicators.note: something adapted has been changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: eras are periods of time
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper advert adapted to promote a cult movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is ERAS; only 'here' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Eraserhead is David Lynch's 1977 debut feature, a surreal midnight-movie favourite.

clue.text: Scandinavian with a fishy protuberance in the ear

indicators.note: what is heard in the ear is a sound, so we want a word that sounds alike

blocks.note: a fin sticks out from a fish's body

explanation.surface: A Nordic person with something odd growing in their ear.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, Finland is Nordic rather than Scandinavian, but the looser use is common.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a native of Finland, loosely grouped with the Scandinavian peoples.

clue.text: Give weapons to old mafioso? That would be a spectacular ending

blocks.note: to arm someone is to give them weapons
aged means old
a don is a Mafia boss

explanation.surface: Arming an elderly gangster would end in a bloodbath.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the biblical final battle, used for any catastrophic, world-ending finale.

clue.text: They amend all characters alternately in liturgical text

indicators.note: taking characters alternately means keeping every other letter of the words

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Editors who go through every letter of a church text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They amend' looks like a definition of editors, but these words are only the letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a book of hymns used in church services.

clue.text: Fog, like gravity, is confusing

blocks.note: mist is a thin fog
akin means similar, like
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Remarks that fog, like the physics of gravity, is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' is a verb here, as in confusing one thing for another, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaking one thing for another means confusing the two, so the participles swap cleanly.

clue.text: How a wheat farmer might refer to a crop out loud: "It's a headache!"

indicators.note: said out loud, the phrase is heard rather than read, so we want a word sounding the same

blocks.clueFragment: How a wheat farmer might refer to a crop
blocks.note: a wheat farmer would call the crop my grain

explanation.surface: A farmer complaining that the harvest is a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe, recurring kind of headache, often with nausea.

clue.text: Look into cuts in waterproof footwear

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
gashes are deep cuts

explanation.surface: Checking for slits in rubber boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Galoshes are rubber overshoes worn to keep ordinary shoes dry in wet weather.

clue.text: Frenetically spur team toward the source

indicators.note: frenetic means wild and frantic, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coach urging a team on, perhaps rowers heading for the river's origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream means moving against the current, back toward where a river begins.

clue.text: Brownback's a snake holding this back!

definitions.note: possessive: the state that is Brownback's

indicators.note: the words hold the answer within them, so it is concealed in a run of letters
back tells us to read the concealed letters in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A jibe calling politician Sam Brownback a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Brownback was a senator and then governor of Kansas; the exclamation mark flags the clue's cheek. 'Brownback's' belongs both to the definition and to the letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownback represented and governed Kansas, so his state is the one named.

clue.text: Engineer opens municipal center without a guarantee

indicators.note: to engineer is to rework and rebuild, so these letters are reconstructed in a new order
the center of a word is its middle, so only the letter in the exact middle is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the fifth of its nine letters

explanation.surface: An engineer opening a city hall with no warranty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a person, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done on spec is done speculatively, with no promise of payment or acceptance.

clue.text: Sausage for a difficult child

blocks.note: first meaning: short for bratwurst, a German pork sausage
second meaning: a badly behaved youngster

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a treat offered to a fussy child; each half names the word on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a casual name for a German grilling sausage and an insult for an unruly kid.

clue.text: Misguided petition as Christmastime staple

indicators.note: misguided means sent the wrong way, so these letters end up out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wrong-headed petition treated as a regular feature of the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia, with its red bracts, is the potted plant sold everywhere in December.

clue.text: Steak consumption unit

blocks.note: consumption is the old name for tuberculosis, TB
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: How much steak a person eats, measured in portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumption' suggests eating, which suits steak, but it is the old name for the lung disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bone is a beef cut with a T-shaped bone separating the sirloin and tenderloin.

clue.text: Mountain capital is home to historic civilization

indicators.note: a place that is home to something houses it, so the answer lives inside these words

blocks.note: the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A high-altitude capital, like Cuzco, housing an ancient people.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the Inca capital Cuzco sat high in the Andes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca built a vast Andean empire that fell to Spanish conquest in the 1530s.

clue.text: I nosh upon crackers where the workers are organized

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so these letters go haywire into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone snacking on crackers in a workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like the snack being eaten but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A union shop is a workplace where employees must join a labor union, so its staff are unionized.

clue.text: Leaders in Delhi and Islamabad are separated by fashionable loincloth

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so we keep the opening letter of each word
two things separated by a third have it placed between them

blocks.note: first letter of the word
first letter of the word
what is hot is in fashion

explanation.surface: The leaders of India and Pakistan kept apart by a trendy garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two cities; HOT goes between their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the wrapped cloth worn round the waist and legs by many men in South Asia.

clue.text: Party machinery designates a spot to return to

definitions.text: designates a spot to return to

blocks.note: a do is a party
gears are the toothed wheels of a machine

explanation.surface: A political party's apparatus marking a place to revisit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party machinery' reads as one political phrase, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog-ear a book is to fold down a page corner so the reader can find that page again.

clue.text: Hide, formerly, in a Western university

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: once means at some former time
Cal is the nickname of the University of California, Berkeley

explanation.surface: An animal skin, once kept at a college in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a noun, an animal pelt, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to keep it out of sight, a direct synonym of the verb.
